candidates.statement: \ref{prop:CFcommFrob} gives the existence of commutative Frobenius relations among CF generators. We would like to know if they are sufficient-- namely, are there other necessary relations if one wants to give a presentation of the category $\operatorname{Cob}( 3)_{S^2,CF} $? This section introduces a tool which we call \textit{local models of failures}, which the next section uses alongside theorem \ref{thm:Cob2Cob3CFIso} to prove sufficiency.

candidates.statement: \ref{generate} shows that $G_2 $ is generating. We need to show that the relations listed above are sufficient. Let $[M]$ be a bordism, and $f_0, f_1:M\to \mathbb{R}$ admissible excellent Morse functions inducing two generating compositions. We claim that there is a path from $f_0$ to $f_1$ which exhibits finitely many prime-commutativity relations, co/legs and co/waist relations, or fails to be excellent Morse at finitely many times due to commutative Frobenius relations. Thus the two compositions of $[M]$ are related by a sequence of prime relations and commutative Frobenius relations.
